problem_statement:
Add `java.lang.Comparable` in set of "unsafe" polymorphic base types [CVE-2026-83557]

`DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator` blocks polymorphic handling for a set of "unsafe" base types -- types with such a wide range of implementations that allowing all subtypes offers essentially no protection (`Object`, `Serializable`, `Closeable`, `AutoCloseable`, `Cloneable`, `Runnable` (2.19+), `java.util.logging.Handler`, `javax.naming.Referenceable`, `javax.sql.DataSource`).

`java.lang.Comparable` is missing from that set, although it is implemented by a very wide range of JDK and application types, comparable in breadth to `Serializable`. So a property declared as `Comparable` with `@JsonTypeInfo` (and no explicitly configured `PolymorphicTypeValidator`) will accept a type id for essentially any class implementing `Comparable`.

Reported via GHSA-gx83-3vf8-gh7j.

Note: in 2.x `DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator` is only used if `MapperFeature.BLOCK_UNSAFE_POLYMORPHIC_BASE_TYPES` is enabled (default validator being `LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator`); in 3.x it is the default validator.
